source.title: UniFed: A Unified Framework for Federated Learning on Non-IID Image Features
source.authors: Mei-Rui Jiang; Xiaoxiao Li; Xiaofei Zhang; Michael Kamp; Qianming Dou

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether batch-normalization changes federated training convergence and performance, using client-specific BN in non-IID federated image classification rather than the centralized setups named in V6.
record.gate_note: The paper compares federated algorithms with and without client-specific BN and reports convergence and accuracy outcomes. Theoretical claims and cited results are not cataloged as empirical rows.
record.test_reason: UniFed compares client-specific BN with aggregated BN; both conditions contain BN. Its convergence results measure the benefit of keeping BN local in federated learning, not the effect of adding BN versus training without it required by V6. The theoretical comparison also uses BN in both conditions. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that client-specific BN improves federated convergence and internal-client performance, and improves external-client generalization through test-specific statistics. Their theoretical guarantees compare client-specific BN with aggregated BN.
record.recipe_differences: Federated learning on non-IID image features with client-specific BN kept local; the claim version concerns adding BN in centralized classification settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that some methods, including MOON and PerFedAvg, can show late-round overfitting without the strategy, while client-specific BN maintains a stable training trend. It reports convergence gains for almost all tested algorithms.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1.2 reports faster average training-loss convergence for almost all eight federated algorithms and lower converged loss with client-specific rather than aggregated BN. Section 3.3 provides a corresponding theoretical comparison for overparameterized two-layer ReLU networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under non-IID client feature distributions, retaining client-specific BN instead of aggregating BN can accelerate federated training.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 2–3 and Section 4.2 report improved internal and external client test accuracy; external testing uses re-estimated client-specific BN statistics. These measure prediction performance rather than the BN-versus-no-BN training-speed effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Client-specific BN can improve federated prediction accuracy under client feature shifts, including on unseen clients through test-time statistics estimation.

record.problems: Convergence curves are figure-only and no per-method numeric convergence values or uncertainty estimates are given. The text says 'almost all' algorithms but does not identify exceptions.
record.rows_left_out: No CIFAR-10-C internal test-accuracy table rows were extracted: those are final test accuracy, not training speed, the behavior measured by V6. Medical-dataset results are stated as accuracy improvements but do not report convergence speed.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large randomly initialized convolutional networks, including random labels and size or recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Recovery above initial stability limits, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
Adding BN versus otherwise comparable networks without BN, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's comparison with normalized residual networks.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains Figure 3's caption and narrative but no readable per-algorithm curves. Consequently, the reported benefit for almost all algorithms cannot justify eight individual observed states. This uncertainty does not itself challenge any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error, corrupted or random labels, and model size or training duration.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects, plain versus residual networks, and training error.
Initialization choices and trainable depth in plain networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature, and divergence.
The paper tests federated image classification with client-specific BN, not the listed centralized sigmoid/MNIST, VGG/CIFAR-10, or Inception/ImageNet settings. It does not test Fixup.

rows.baseline: Original algorithm without client-specific BN; figure only
rows.note: The text says the strategy clearly improves average convergence speed for almost all algorithms; the plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: FedAvg is an algorithm, not a model. The baseline uses aggregated BN, not a network without BN. This method comparison cannot establish V6; the supplied figure text also does not identify individual convergence-speed exceptions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Eight tested federated algorithms on internal CIFAR-10-C clients
reader_labels.reason: The authors report clearly improved average convergence speed for almost all methods and lower converged loss; rows R1–R8 record the figure-only comparisons. The text does not specify which methods, so this label applies to the reported group rather than asserting every row individually.
